trust_decision.summary: DefaultParameterFormatter.format chooses the string-literal escaper from the statement's leading keyword: only SELECT/WITH/INSERT/UPDATE/MERGE get Trino quote-doubling, and every other statement (including Trino-engine DELETE and CTAS) gets Hive backslash escaping, which Trino does not treat as an escape, so a quote in a parameter ends the literal.

landing_point.why: The advisory names DefaultParameterFormatter plus DELETE/CTAS; the prefix tuple that picks the escaper is the obvious first line to read, and the escaper is chosen nowhere else.

fix_sites.entry_point: Cursor.execute(operation, parameters) -> BaseCursor._execute -> _prepare_query -> self._formatter.format (pyathena/cursor.py:85, pyathena/common.py:674, pyathena/common.py:743)
fix_sites.module_kind: core library formatter (shared by all cursor types, sync and aio, and the SQLAlchemy dialect)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix diff holds only a merge-commit header with no hunks (fix.diff:1-2), so the published change cannot be seen. The only escaper-selection code in the tree is pyathena/formatter.py:271-275.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory lists only DELETE and CTAS, and non-DML statements legitimately need Hive escaping (ALTER TABLE ADD/DROP PARTITION, tests/pyathena/test_formatter.py:11-47). A solver can argue that EXPLAIN/VALUES/CREATE VIEW/UNLOAD, or a statement starting with a comment or parenthesis, is 'not DELETE/CTAS' or an unusual form, and leave the prefix check alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Hive-engine DDL (ALTER TABLE ... ADD/DROP PARTITION, CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE, MSCK, SHOW/DESCRIBE) must keep Hive backslash escaping, and CREATE TABLE without AS (Hive DDL) must stay on the Hive escaper even though it shares the CREATE TABLE prefix with CTAS. A fix that always uses the Presto escaper, or treats any CREATE TABLE as Trino, breaks DDL literals that contain backslashes or quotes.

O6_input_shapes: str inside list/tuple/set, escaped with the same escaper (pyathena/formatter.py:192-215, pyathena/formatter.py:232-234)
Decimal is passed through the escaper but holds only digits (pyathena/formatter.py:218-220)
statement-prefix variants: leading whitespace is stripped but comments/parentheses are not (pyathena/formatter.py:269-272)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Trino-engine statements outside the prefix tuple (EXPLAIN, VALUES, CREATE VIEW ... AS, UNLOAD, PREPARE/EXECUTE ... USING) fall through to the Hive escaper
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names only DELETE/CTAS; these are less common statement types
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same line as the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A DML/CTAS statement that starts with a SQL comment or an opening parenthesis fails startswith() and gets the Hive escaper
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Leading comments look like an edge case outside 'DELETE/CTAS'

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The DDL compiler's COMMENT escaping is hard-coded Hive-style; a CTAS/view compiler path reusing it under the Trino engine would be the same mechanism
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding SQLAlchemy CTAS or view support would plausibly reuse _escape_comment from the existing DDL compiler.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: wrap_unload could take a user-supplied location/format value and embed it with the Hive escaper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: UNLOAD is Trino-engine; adding parameterised options there would naturally reuse the module's escapers.

O9_family: SQL injection (CWE-89): dialect-mismatched string-literal escaping chosen by a statement-prefix classifier

O10_build.project_tests: tests/pyathena/test_formatter.py tests the pure formatter, but tests/pyathena/conftest.py:14-18 uploads to S3 and creates Athena databases at session start, so the project's own suite needs AWS. Hidden tests must call DefaultParameterFormatter without that conftest.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add "DELETE" and "CREATE TABLE" to the startswith tuple at pyathena/formatter.py:272. This also moves Hive CREATE TABLE DDL to Presto escaping and still misses EXPLAIN/VALUES/comment-prefixed statements.
